thread:
alex: Morning handoff — quick summary of the last 6h before I sign off. Observability spike at ~02:10 UTC, followed by elevated 5xxs for a subset of regional routed requests. No full outage but some sustained client retries.

incident-bot: [pager] HIGH: increased 5xx rate (>2% p95) for /v1/generate in eu-west-1. Pager #9241. Affected customers: 3 (partial). Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/9241

alex: What happened: route-selector started misclassifying some long-tail requests as "low-priority" during a control-plane config rollout (feature flag rollback yesterday). That caused extra queuing on the lower-tier path and hit the rate limiter hard.

mira: Got it. Any mitigation already applied?

alex: Yes — at 02:22 I manually pinned route-selector to previous release and bumped the per-route concurrency for the affected pool. Also enabled a temporary fast-path rule for known high-SLA customers. Error rate dropped to ~0.6% by 02:34.

samir: Logs/observability notes: saw queue depth spike on pool-3 workers and a correlated rise in tokenization latency. Trace samples: some requests retried twice before succeeding. Important traces saved under: /traces/2026-03-16/9241 (internal link).

jess: Customer impact intel: Two paying customers (tier: enterprise) reported timeouts on webhook callbacks, but requests eventually succeeded after client retries. No billing complaints yet, CS pinged both with note and ETA for RCA.

mira: OK. For the handoff: I'm taking primary for the next 8h. Samir — you stay secondary?

samir: Affirmative. I'll watch the routing and rate-limiter dashboards.

alex: Hand-off checklist I recommend:
- Watch these dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/route-selector, https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rl-rate-limiter
- Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/route-selector-rollback (steps 1–4 are the quick rollback)
- Temp mitigations: pin route-selector, increase per-route concurrency, fast-path rule (only for high-sla)
- If 5xx > 1.5% for >10m: escalate to eng-runtime oncall and open short bridge (use /start-bridge in #eng-oncall)

incident-bot: Note: Runbook step 2 requires cluster-admin permissions. A record of who performed manual pinning is attached to the incident.

mira: Current status at handoff: 5xx steady at 0.5%, queue depth normalizing, no new pagers in last 50m. CS follow-ups scheduled for 11:00 UTC.

alex: Known follow-ups / outstanding items for next shift:
- RCA: check why control-plane rollout allowed misclassification (possible flapping flag gating).
- Add an automated smoke-check after route-selector rollouts to validate tail-classification distribution.
- Consider rate-limiter backpressure metrics to trigger earlier fallback rather than letting queue depth climb.

mira: I'll open a ticket for the smoke-test (ENG-ops-1428) and add a postmortem note to incident 9241.

samir: If anything spikes, I'll start the bridge. Contact chain: ping me -> jess -> eng-runtime lead (oncall paging).

jess: FYI: CS wants a short summary for customers by EOD. I'll draft and send after final RCA note.

alex: Thanks team — leaving a few quick commands for the new primary in case you need them: 
```
# pin route-selector to previous release
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/route-selector route-selector=registry/redwood/route-selector:v2.13.7
# bump per-route concurrency
redis-cli -h rate-limiter-ctrl HSET route:eu-west-1:per_route_concurrency 200
```

mira: Copy that. I'll monitor for the next 30m and then take standard checks every hour. Taking over now — good handoff. :thumbsup:

alex: Appreciate it. Signing off.

incident-bot: Incident 9241 status updated -> monitoring. Postmortem pending.
